title: Bind each Bun test's Acceptance/WMBT header to a URN the plan declares

facts.note: Bun stack realization; only Bun test files are checked.
Any existing Bun test file carrying a `// Acceptance:` or `// WMBT:` header, whether or not it is touched by the current change.

Repository lookup scope, NOT an edited-file selector: declared URNs are collected from plan/**. Additionally, a change touching plan/** (e.g. an acceptance rename) must re-trigger the check over all existing Bun test bindings.
Either side of the binding changing can break resolution; diff-level observer needed to recognise both.

Repository-level detector finding: a header URN not stated anywhere under plan/**. The repository-level precondition (plan declares at least one acceptance) is evaluated by this detector, not by a task-level fact.

fires: A Bun test header `// Acceptance: acc:...` names a URN that appears nowhere under plan/**.
A Bun test header `// WMBT: wmbt:...` names a WMBT that the plan never mentions.
A plan-only change renames an acceptance and existing, untouched Bun test headers still carry the old URN.
doesNotFire: A Bun test carrying no binding header at all (owned by tester.bun.acceptance-binding-declared).
A repository whose plan declares no acceptances at all (NOT_APPLICABLE).
A header whose URN is stated anywhere in the plan, under any key in wagon, feature or WMBT documents.

given: The repository's plan declares acceptances and a Bun test carries an `// Acceptance:` or `// WMBT:` binding header
when: the binding is checked (test or header changed, plan changed, or any CI run)
then: Every `// Acceptance:` and `// WMBT:` URN in the header MUST be stated somewhere under plan/**.
prefer: Repair the binding from the plan, not the plan from the test: the plan is authoritative during test authoring.

Stale header or renamed acceptance: point the test at the declared acceptance it actually exercises and proves (illustrative: `// Acceptance: acc:<wagon>:<ID>` where that URN is stated in a plan/<wagon>/ document; `// WMBT: wmbt:<wagon>:<WMBT>`).
Test proves different behavior: bind it to that behavior's existing declared acceptance; if it does not prove the claimed acceptance, adjust the test, not the label.
No declared acceptance fits: return to the authorized planning flow so the behavior is declared deliberately before the test claims coverage.
avoid: Creating, renaming or repurposing a plan acceptance, or inventing one, merely to make a test resolve or clear this finding; plan additions are planner work justified by the behavior.
Binding to a convenient but semantically unrelated declared acceptance (the dangerous gaming case).
unless: The plan declares no acceptances at all: NOT_APPLICABLE.
The test has no binding header: owned by tester.bun.acceptance-binding-declared (no double-count).
why: A binding to an acceptance that exists nowhere attributes the test to nothing, making coverage figures fiction: a NAME accepted where a CLAIM is required. Strict (severity 4): a finding is not suppressible and fails CI (see shared:policy.strict-disposition).
evidence: The detector collects every `acc:`/`wmbt:` URN token under plan/** and reports zero Bun test headers naming a URN absent from that set.

Reviewer confirms each header's acceptance is the one the test case genuinely exercises and asserts (resolution is only the structural half of truth; a resolving header is still semantically false if the case exercises or asserts something else).
Diff shows no plan acceptance created, renamed or repurposed solely to make an existing test resolve.
verifier_detail: Resolves each Bun test's declared binding against the plan: collect every `acc:` / `wmbt:` URN stated anywhere under `plan/**`, then flag a test whose `// Acceptance:` or `// WMBT:` header names one the plan never mentions.

Declared URNs are read as TOKENS rather than parsed structurally, on purpose: acceptances are stated under several keys across wagon, feature and WMBT documents, and a reference resolves if the plan states that URN anywhere. Over-accepting is the safe direction — the failure caught is a reference to something the plan never mentions.

Return NOT_APPLICABLE when the consumer declares no acceptances at all: a repository with no plan has nothing to resolve against, and reporting there would fire on every unplanned project rather than on a broken reference.
Do not report tests with no binding header (sibling tester.bun.acceptance-binding-declared owns presence; reporting both would double-count one defect).

Implemented as member of the `bun_tester_discipline_detector` FAMILY detector (checks/t_acceptance_resolves.mjs). Core owns the shape of acceptance/WMBT artifacts; only a per-stack detector can see whether a Bun test resolves into them.
Term resolvable_binding: an `// Acceptance:` or `// WMBT:` header whose URN is stated somewhere in the consumer's plan, so the test is attributable to a declared obligation rather than to a name.
Diagnostic hint: a renamed acceptance is the common mechanical cause; a convenient but semantically unrelated acceptance is the dangerous gaming case.
Disposition strict, severity 4: a test bound to an artifact that does not exist is not suppressible and fails CI.

Source fix-hint example (verbatim, illustrative of a resolving header): `// URN: test:orders:checkout:E001-SMOKE-001-renders-row` / `// Acceptance: acc:orders:E001-SMOKE-001-renders-row   # stated in plan/orders/E001.yaml` / `// WMBT: wmbt:orders:E001`.
audit: Original name: A test's Acceptance / WMBT binding names an artifact the plan declares (Bun)

Lineage: sibling tester.bun.acceptance-binding-declared asks only whether a header is PRESENT, which a test satisfies by naming anything at all. Measured on a consumer, a test bound to `acc:does-not-exist:E999-NEVER-DECLARED` passed every gated rule in this workspace — the recurring defect this hub keeps finding: a NAME accepted where a CLAIM is required. The two rules are complementary — one requires the binding to exist, this one requires it to be true.
Source fix-hint example used application-specific names (orders/checkout/E001); kept verbatim in verifier_detail[8], generalized in prefer[1].

splitSuggestion.then: A test bound to a declared acceptance MUST actually exercise and assert that acceptance's behavior; when it does not, adjust the test rather than the label.

sharedNodes.text: strict: a finding from a strict rule is not suppressible and fails CI.

additions.text: Semantic truth of a resolving binding (the case genuinely proves the acceptance) is an independent, LLM-judged obligation; suggest separate convention tester.bun.binding-semantically-proves-acceptance. Then is limited to structural resolution; semantic repair guidance is kept in prefer/avoid/evidence.
additions.justification: Rule 2: one obligation in then; source contains both structural resolution and semantic truth.

additions.text: Activation 'change' values (binding header edited; plan acceptance renamed/removed) and the when clause 'any CI run' make the check apply to all existing bindings, including after plan-only changes.
additions.justification: Source checks every Bun test binding against the plan (repository-level detector, fails CI); a plan rename can break an untouched test. Phrasing maps that scope to activation vocabulary.

additions.text: prefer[1] uses a neutral placeholder example (`acc:<wagon>:<ID>`, plan/<wagon>/) instead of the source's application-specific orders example, which is kept verbatim in verifier_detail[8].
additions.justification: Rule 4: codebase-neutral coder text, without losing the source snippet.
